description: We are a team of three with backgrounds in biology, programming, and design. We combine biological knowledge to understand astronauts’ health data, Rust programming skills to build our solution, and design skills to create clear, easy-to-use interfaces. Together, we aim to unlock our potential and turn bold ideas into meaningful solutions for healthier lives in space.
summary:
KOOK (Kinetic Observation & Optimal Keel) is a health monitoring dashboard designed to help astronauts independently manage their health during long-duration space missions. During long-duration space missions, astronauts are exposed to five major health hazards identified by NASA. As these risks vary in severity, astronauts need a system that enables immediate health assessment and provides step-by-step guidance. KOOK enables efficient health assessments by comparing baseline health data collected on Earth with real-time accumulated health data collected in space. KOOK categorizes biomarkers severity into three levels: Urgent, Potential, and Normal.
Astronauts can access the Health Instruction Library, where medical professionals have uploaded health guidelines. A Linked audio device also provides voice-guided instructions, allowing astronauts to follow the recommended steps without relying solely on the screen. When further medical support is needed, astronauts can communicate directly with Earth-based medical professionals through one-on-one chat consultations. By helping astronauts understand their health conditions and take appropriate action independently, KOOK empowers them to take a more active role in managing their well-being during long-duration space missions.
details:
How does it work

KOOK enables efficient health assessments by comparing baseline health data collected on Earth with real-time accumulated health data collected in space.

Step 1: Immediate Response

KOOK categorizes biomarkers severity into three levels: Urgent, Potential, and Normal.

Astronauts can access the Health Instruction Library, where medical professionals have uploaded health guidelines. A Linked audio device also provides voice-guided instructions, allowing astronauts to follow the recommended steps without relying solely on the screen.

Step 2: In-Depth Consultation

When further medical support is needed, astronauts can communicate directly with Earth-based medical professionals through one-on-one chat consultations.

Why It Matters

By helping astronauts understand their health conditions and take appropriate action independently, KOOK empowers them to take a more active role in managing their well-being during long-duration space missions. Astronauts in various fields can easily monitor and manage their health status.

What Tools We Used 

Planning - Notion, Google Docs, draw.io
Data collection and analysis - Claude, ChatGPT
Design - Figma
Development - JavaScript, HTML, CSS

Use of SI
Claude: Used to apply UI icons and components consistently across the interface, and to write and review code.

ChatGPT: Used to select the biomarkers and set the threshold ranges for each status level.

Edge of Our Team

Our team's greatest strength is the way we bring together different perspectives and skills. With backgrounds in biology, programming, and design, each of us approaches problems differently, but we share the same goal: making space health management more accessible and practical for astronauts.

Considered Values

We believe that technology should not make health management more complicated. It should make it easier for people to understand their condition and know what to do next.

Throughout the development of KOOK, we focused on three values:

Accessibility: Health information should be understandable even to people without medical expertise.

Real-time: Health data is continuously monitored and updated, allowing astronauts and medical professionals on Earth to stay informed about changes in the astronaut's health status and communicate.

Expertise’s advice: No matter where astronauts are in space, they can consult with medical professionals on Earth through direct communication.
